author: logangraham
text: @quantumVerd Human capital investment + capital investment -> productivity growth -> e.g. cheap healthcare w/ better outcomes, exporting carbon capture & storage, a brand new psychotherapeutics industry. But we won't make it if our growth comes just from real estate & financialization.

author: logangraham
text: @quantumVerd Economic growth is simultaneously more boring and more exciting than that. More boring: driving towards economy-wide productivity improvement across every industry is where the magic happens. More exciting: we can make magic happen.
In sum: let's build a positive vision of where our country can be, and let's work to get there.

The good news: the answer to the question is also the thing that achieves this. It also has the very, very convenient side effect of producing more and better jobs, per dollar spent, over the long run.

We strive to decarbonise our economy. We strive to export low- and zero-carbon energy. We strive to grow through bold innovation that takes care of *every human being in Canada*. We strive to be the healthiest, happiest, most empowered country in the world.

For my fellow Canadian citizens, unironically, the question asked in this tweet is the question we should be asking. Rachel sees this as a negative, and I see this is as a positive. Let's build this vision and rally around it. https://t.co/Uo1CigseUr

author: logangraham
text: For a bunch of people whose jobs are to speculate wildly on unspecified, hard science, they do an amazing job at either (a) having their finger on the future's pulse or (b) confirming my biases.

author: logangraham
text: Last, I completely missed their other moonshots in machine learning. As ever, I'm impressed by their ability to nail down the machine learning frontiers we're just grappling with: robustness, weak/semi supervision, theory (rather than alchemy), lifelong learning. https://t.co/qsYdu8fcyI

author: logangraham
text: Then there's the moonshot of Automating Science. If we found a general way to do this, it might end up being the most prosperity-producing tool invented in this century. Imagine dark factories (orbiting in space, even!) that report back ever so often with new science. https://t.co/ftbFcmI4Cr

author: logangraham
text: Similarly, they want to figure out build a system for learning to model *any* system without bias. This is the meta-problem, named "Big Mechanism". It's like recreating the process of how humans come to understand systems – our multi-hundred year journey of science. https://t.co/yqK9IU22x8

author: logangraham
text: Modeling the World – their program is literally called "World Modelers". Humanity is a bunch of complex intersecting systems – economic, transportation, information, biological. We should build causal simulations of them all coming together. (right: focus on social systems) https://t.co/bfAg2hX0ZQ

text: @oughtinc I hung out with Ought on Friday and was impressed by their vision. They are simultaneously pushing the frontier in machine learning – factored cognition is cool – and in research, as an independent nonprofit research group with a startup vibe in the heart of SF.

author: logangraham
text: Machine learning / software engineers: here's a chance to lead engineering at @oughtinc. If you want to work on (a) societally meaningful technology (b) exciting, frontier technology, this is a great chance. https://t.co/rXibhz3eS9

author: logangraham
text: @joininteract Especially interested in encouraging people who are (one of) underrepresented, nontraditional, geographically non-US/Canada, deep moral thinkers, self-doubting, cynical. Would love to see more artists, journalists, farmers, small-towners, just getting started.

author: logangraham
text:
My yearly @joininteract tweet: if you are between 18 and 23 and you care about how technology can/should do good in the world, apply.

This year, I'm open to video calling 1-on-1 with people who are (a) not an insider to the Valley world (b) have barriers to applying/exposure.
